levels.label: Beginner
levels.blurb: Small, finished tools that each teach one core skill. You build something that runs, and you learn to publish it properly.

projects.title: Network Reconnaissance Tool
projects.summary: A Python command line scanner that finds open TCP ports on a host you own and reports what is listening.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository containing the scanner, a sample JSON report from a scan of your own machine, tests, and a README that explains the tool and the legal limits of scanning.

projects.title: Password Security Analyzer
projects.summary: A tool that scores password strength with real rules, checks a local wordlist, and never stores or transmits the passwords it sees.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with the analyzer, a command line interface, a test suite, and a README that explains how the score is calculated and why passwords are never stored.

projects.title: Network Traffic Investigation
projects.summary: Investigate a packet capture of a suspicious incident, write the timeline and findings, and automate the first pass with a Python script.
skills: Reading protocols such as DNS, HTTP and TCP
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with an investigation report in Markdown, the extraction script, the extracted data, and screenshots, all without the raw capture if its licence does not allow redistribution.

projects.title: Security Log Analyzer
projects.summary: A Python tool that parses authentication and web server logs, finds suspicious patterns such as brute force attempts, and produces a report.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with the parser, the detection rules, sample logs, a generated report, tests and a README explaining each rule and its false positive risks.

levels.label: Intermediate
levels.blurb: Projects that combine several skills on realistic data and ask you to make design decisions of your own.

projects.title: Web Application Security Assessment
projects.summary: Assess a deliberately vulnerable web application you run yourself, document each finding with evidence and write remediation advice.
tools: Burp Suite Community or OWASP ZAP
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with an assessment report, evidence screenshots, a finding register and a short remediation plan, without any exploit that works against real systems.

projects.title: SIEM Detection Lab
projects.summary: Build a small SIEM, ingest logs from real sources, write detection rules, and prove they fire by running safe attack simulations.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with the lab setup instructions, the detection rules as code, a detection catalogue mapped to ATT&CK, test evidence for each rule, dashboard exports and a README.

projects.title: Cloud Security Posture Checker
projects.summary: A Python tool that scans a cloud account for risky configuration such as public storage and over broad permissions, and reports findings with fixes.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with the checker, Terraform for the intentionally misconfigured test resources, sample findings output, tests and a README with the least privilege policy the tool needs.

projects.title: SOC Alert Dashboard
projects.summary: A web dashboard where analysts see alerts, triage them with context, and record decisions, backed by a small API and database.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with the API, the database model, the dashboard, sample alerts, tests, screenshots and a README that explains the triage workflow.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.blurb: Engineering projects that integrate earlier work, include automated testing and ask you to defend your choices.

projects.title: Detection Engineering Pipeline
projects.summary: Treat detections as software: write Sigma rules, test them against labelled data in continuous integration, and measure their quality.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with at least ten Sigma rules, labelled test data, a test harness, a CI workflow that passes, a generated coverage report and documentation of the contribution process.

projects.title: Cloud Attack Path Analyzer
projects.summary: Model cloud identities and resources as a graph and find the chains of permissions an attacker could use to reach sensitive data.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with the analyzer, a sample environment export, Terraform for a sandbox with planted paths, ranked findings, diagrams of the paths, tests and a README.

projects.title: Automated Incident Response Pipeline
projects.summary: Receive an alert, enrich it, decide on a response, and act with human approval and a full audit trail, in a safe sandbox.
tools: A job queue or background tasks
A chat webhook or email in a test workspace
AWS sandbox or a local mock
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repository with the pipeline, playbooks as code, a sandbox target, an audit log sample, tests including failure cases, an architecture diagram and a README with a safety design section.

levels.label: Job Ready
levels.blurb: A flagship project you can talk about for most of an interview, built and documented like real work.

projects.title: End to End Cloud Security Operations Platform
projects.summary: Your flagship project: a small security operations platform that detects, investigates and responds across a cloud environment, documented like a real engineering project.
tools: Draw.io or a similar diagram tool
projects.deliverable: A public repository with infrastructure as code, integrated components, a threat model, an architecture diagram, a runbook, a cost estimate, test evidence, a recorded incident walkthrough and a README written for a hiring manager.

featured.title: Network Reconnaissance Tool
featured.summary: A Python command line scanner that finds open TCP ports on a host you own and reports what is listening.
featured.deliverable: A GitHub repository containing the scanner, a sample JSON report from a scan of your own machine, tests, and a README that explains the tool and the legal limits of scanning.
criteria: I ran the scanner against a machine I own and saved the output.
My results match Nmap for the same port range, or I can explain every difference.
The tool refuses to scan an address I did not confirm.
Automated tests run and pass on a clean checkout.
The README explains how to run it and states the legal limits of scanning.
interview: Explain what happens at the network level when your scanner checks a port that is open, closed and filtered.
Why does a full connect scan get noticed more easily than a SYN scan, and why did you choose a connect scan?
How did you decide the number of worker threads and the timeout?
A scan reports port 8080 filtered but the service is running. What could explain it?
How would a defender detect your scanner, and what would they see in their logs?
What legal and ethical rules did you build into the tool, and why?
featured.cv_bullet: Built a concurrent Python TCP port scanner with banner grabbing and JSON reporting, validated against Nmap results and tested with automated unit tests.
